about: Chapter 7, Shapes and Patterns: 68 patterns, three or four for each of the 15 skills (1 and 2 marks), three 3-mark and three 5-mark long answers in steps (#208), and three 4-mark case studies, drawn from the chapter's 500 questions. Only what words alone state fully is generated (no pictures). All DRAFT until Ashalatha approves them.

patterns.text: A paper strip is woven in the order {u.t}, and the order then repeats. Is move {k} over or under?
patterns.answer: (u.m1 if (k - 1) % u.L == 0 else (u.m2 if (k - 1) % u.L == 1 else (u.m3 if (k - 1) % u.L == 2 else u.m4)))
patterns.hint: Find the repeating unit. Divide the move number by the length of the unit and look at the remainder.
patterns.explanation: The unit has {u.L} moves. Move {k} is move {(k - 1) % u.L + 1} of a unit, so it is {(u.m1 if (k - 1) % u.L == 0 else (u.m2 if (k - 1) % u.L == 1 else (u.m3 if (k - 1) % u.L == 2 else u.m4)))}.
patterns.misconception: Copies visible symbols without identifying the repeating unit or restarts the rule at the wrong place.
patterns.notes: Units of 2 to 4 moves (over/under, never all the same, always the smallest unit); move 7 to 40. Answer: over or under.

patterns.text: The weaving unit '{u.d}' is repeated {t} times. How many '{w.w}' moves are made?
patterns.hint: Count the '{w.w}' moves in one unit, then multiply by the number of repeats.
patterns.explanation: One unit has {u.co if w.w == 'over' else u.cu} '{w.w}' moves. {t} repeats have {t} × {u.co if w.w == 'over' else u.cu} = {t * (u.co if w.w == 'over' else u.cu)}.
patterns.misconception: Copies visible symbols without identifying the repeating unit or restarts the rule at the wrong place.
patterns.notes: Units of 2 to 4 moves repeated 3 to 12 times; asks for over or under moves.

patterns.text: A woven row has {m} moves and repeats a unit of {ln} moves. How many complete units are in the row?
patterns.hint: A complete unit needs all {ln} moves. Divide and ignore what is left over.
patterns.explanation: {m} ÷ {ln} = {m // ln} remainder {m % ln}, so there are {m // ln} complete units.
patterns.misconception: Copies visible symbols without identifying the repeating unit or restarts the rule at the wrong place.
patterns.notes: Units of 3 to 6 moves; rows of 13 to 60 moves, never an exact number of units.
